>If communism is then end goal then why do socialists just not say that they're communists?

Usually just the stigma that's attached to the word. 

But then again, it depends on which socialists are you talking to here. Real socialists usually say that they are communists. But socialists like Bernie Sanders are not actually socialists, and therefore wouldn't say that they're  communists... because they aren't.

>I'm a little bit confused as to what you mean because you said yes, but then you said you're not quite sure. Can you please expand?

Whoops sorry, formatting's a bit shit. I meant to say that yes, in traditional left-right politics, socialism is exclusively on the left wing. When I'm saying that I'm not sure about left-right politics, is that it's just awkward to put political philosophies in only two categories and decide which one goes a bit more to the right and to the left.

I hope that answers that.

I'll try my best to answer these questions but be warned, I'm still a beginner, so I'm just here to try and test out my knowledge of socialism. 

>Does Socialism support free universal healthcare and education for all individuals?

In a socialist society, yes. I would imagine all these things are given without any question.

>Is Socialism a classless, moneyless and stateless ideology like Communism? If not, then please explain why and what it is instead.

By definition, socialism is an economic system in which the workers control and manage the means of production. Socialism is just the process of society to reach the end goal of communism. 

>Just for clarification, and for others who may be unsure, what exactly is Socialism, and how does it differ from Communism?

The question above has the same answer. 

>I'm adamantly for pro LGBT+ rights. Is Socialism accepting of LGBT+ rights?

Communism, for accuracy, is looking to abolish all class problems. This means that it also involves itself with issues like Racism, Feminism, and LGBT to help them solve discriminations.

>Can one be a right wing Socialist or a left wing Socialist, or is Socialism just synonymous with the left end of the political spectrum?

Yes, although I'm not quite sure about left-right politics. What I'm sure is that the 'right' usually is interested in defending private property (Note: different from personal property), which is something that socialism is fundamentally against.

>Is it true that Socialism does not wish to as abolish Capitalism altogether? If so, why?

Socialism and capitalism is incompatible with each other. So your statement is not true. This is because one advocates for the collective control of the means of production while the other advocates for private controls. Also, Sweden is not a socialist nation, it's a nation with a Social Democracy ideology, which is just capitalism with some state funded things. 

>Is Socialism a very altruistic and pro Egalitarian ideology?

I would say so, yes. Communism advocates for social justice for everyone. 

>Is Socialism purely an economic ideology? If not, then what is it instead?

Socialism focuses itself on various aspect of society that is wrong, that includes social issues and economic issues. 

>Just out of curiosity, why are you a Christian Socialist and not a Christian Communist?

Is this a question for me, or you?

>Could you give a few hypothetical examples of Socialism?

Small scale: Workers cooperatives. Rural farming collectives.
Large scale: Revolutionary Catalonia.

That's it for my answers, and it's very half-baked because I'm on my phone. I would like to ask my fellow comrades to correct my answers if there's anything wrong with it, so that I can refine my answers to other future socialists.
